headline: Atlanta wears its city before its team, so sell the A first and let the Hawks ride along.

archetype.name: The Culture Capital's Swing Fans
archetype.description: A Black-led, metro-wide crowd that treats the arena as a runway and Atlanta itself as the team. Loyal in spirit, loud only when the night means something: MLK Day, a big home Cup night, a playoff series.

pulse.teamMoment: Jalen Johnson's Hawks went 46-36 as the No. 6 seed and lost 4-2 to the champion Knicks after leading 2-1. Under Quin Snyder they reloaded around defense with No. 8 pick Kingston Flemings, Lu Dort, Ryan Nembhard, Aaron Wiggins and Devin Carter. Zaccharie Risacher, the 2024 No. 1 pick, went to Dallas.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously optimistic. An All-NBA Johnson, a Most Improved Alexander-Walker and a deep defense give hope. But the 2-1 collapse against New York and the end of the Trae Young chapter keep fans guarded until they see proof.

verifiedMoment: Jalen Johnson's Hawks went defense-first after a 6-seed season. They drafted Kingston Flemings at No. 8 and traded for Lu Dort, Ryan Nembhard, Aaron Wiggins and Devin Carter. Zaccharie Risacher, the 2024 No. 1 pick, went to Dallas.

scorecard.rationale: One of the league's deepest design wells sits on one of its softest fan bases, because Atlanta's pride runs to the city, not the Hawks. Culture is top five, and fandom sits in the bottom quarter (brief scores: opportunity 74, culture 92, retail 64, fandom 52). Atlanta has one of the league's deepest design wells (Black Mecca, hip-hop, HBCU, rink and car culture, an immigrant 770) and a big, style-literate metro. But Hawks fandom runs below the city's cultural heat and arrives in spikes. Retail is broad but car-dependent and split by trade area, and taste gets set in small independent doors whose status needs checking.

headline: Boston backs the banners and doubts the roster: sell heritage, winter gear and neighborhoods, not players

archetype.name: The Banner Counters
archetype.description: A multigenerational fan base that measures itself in titles and treats Celtics history as family property. Loyalty goes to the green, the banners and the parquet first, and to players a distant second. That's exactly what a reset season needs.

pulse.teamMoment: The Tatum-Brown era is over. A 56-26 season ended in a 3-1 first-round collapse to Philadelphia. Brad Stevens then traded Jaylen Brown to the 76ers for Paul George and picks. The rebuild centers on Jayson Tatum, with Mitchell Robinson, Mike Conley and an extended Neemias Queta.
pulse.sentiment: Unsettled and skeptical. Fans are proud of Banner 18, bruised by the collapse and split on the Brown trade. They're wary of George's age and contract, too, after Tatum's father publicly criticized the roster and national free-agency grades panned the summer.

verifiedMoment: The Tatum-Brown era is over. After blowing a 3-1 first-round lead to Philadelphia, Brad Stevens traded Jaylen Brown to the 76ers for Paul George and picks. The roster now runs through Jayson Tatum.

scorecard.rationale: Boston has elite heritage fandom and strong New England retail. Roster doubt after the Brown trade and Nike playing away to New Balance and adidas cap opportunity. Its design well is narrower than the Black-led design capitals' (brief scores: opportunity 76, culture 84, retail 78, fandom 86). Boston pairs one of the league's most intense, heritage-driven fan bases with a deep, distinct civic and neighborhood culture and strong retail: the Garden, Newbury, Concepts and regional outlets. This season, roster doubt and rival brands' home-turf claims cap the opportunity.

opportunities.title: Specter and the Rafters: the heritage layer

opportunities.how: Treat Oct 20-30 as a heritage refresh on product fans can already buy, not a launch. Build the story to work with or without Specter on court on Dec 25. A UV-reactive interior reveals the retired-number row for fans to decode online. Keep the parquet tonal, and tie every graphic to a named Garden reference.
opportunities.segment: Lifelong diehards and holiday gift buyers
opportunities.kpi: Sell-through of heritage pieces versus player pieces at the Pro Shop and Newbury by Dec 26. Specter jersey units in the first confirmed wear week.

handoff.consumer: Lifelong Celtics diehards and holiday gift buyers who back the franchise while they make up their minds about the roster.

headline: Brooklyn was its own city once. Sell the Nets as its team, not New York's other one.

archetype.name: The Borough Separatists
archetype.description: An outnumbered, style-literate tribe that treats the Nets as proof Brooklyn is its own city. Loyalty runs borough first, roster third. It survives losing but punishes anything that reads as Manhattan, tourist or transplant.

pulse.teamMoment: A development year after a 20-62 season. No. 6 pick Mikel Brown Jr. and Egor Demin lead a very young roster, beside veteran scorers Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. and new guard Keon Ellis. Jordi Fernandez is newly extended. There's no opening-night or Christmas Day game.
pulse.sentiment: Patient, wry and mildly hopeful about the kids. Defiantly Brooklyn while the defending-champion Knicks own the city's attention.

verifiedMoment: Still rebuilding, now with more veteran scoring. Julius Randle comes back to New York to join Michael Porter Jr. No. 6 pick Mikel Brown Jr. leads a very young roster under Jordi Fernandez, who just got an extension.

scorecard.rationale: Brooklyn's borough culture and New York retail rank high. After 20-62 in a Knicks title year, Nets fandom is the league's second-thinnest, and the real opportunity is a 2027 build (brief scores: opportunity 66, culture 92, retail 72, fandom 40). Brooklyn's culture is among the deepest and most designable in the league. But the Nets' fandom is thin after 20-62 in a Knicks title year, and most partners and doors are unchecked. The opportunity rests on the borough mark selling without wins. It depends on local co-authorship and a 2027 build, not this season.

headline: Charlotte wears teal as a civic color. Win it with the Hive and the hornet's nest, not a star.

archetype.name: The Homecoming Hive
archetype.description: A loyal, nostalgic two-state fan base whose high point is a building that's gone (the 364-sellout Charlotte Coliseum) and a name it won back. It buys the memory first and the current roster second. It wants to be proven right for staying.

pulse.teamMoment: The LaMelo Ball era is over. Charlotte traded him to Minnesota and handed a 44-38 Play-In team to Brandon Miller and second-year Kon Knueppel, backed by re-signed Coby White, Naz Reid and Grayson Allen. There's no opening-night or Christmas game. The only scheduled national window is the Feb 15 Presidents' Day game, when Ball returns with Minnesota. The Prime Video Play-In and Cup knockouts are contingent second stages.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously hopeful, with a fresh sting. Fans enjoyed the Play-In OT win over Miami, lost at Orlando, then lost their face of the franchise. Analysts split between ESPN's 34-48 projection and David Aldridge's third-best-offseason grade. Heat sits at 56. A winning season and strong offseason grades push it up. The Ball trade, the playoff drought since 2016 and a schedule with no opener or Christmas game pull it back toward the middle.

verifiedMoment: The LaMelo Ball era is over. Charlotte traded him to Minnesota and handed the team to Brandon Miller and second-year Kon Knueppel, with Coby White and Naz Reid in support.

scorecard.rationale: Hive nostalgia is real. But non-Nike faces, one national window and a college-first, mall-and-outlet metro put Charlotte in the bottom fifth on opportunity and fandom and below average on culture and retail (brief scores: opportunity 58, culture 66, retail 52, fandom 50). Charlotte's culture runs deeper, and is less used, than its "Banktown" reputation suggests, and Hive and Hugo nostalgia sell beyond the market. But non-Nike player faces, a single scheduled national window, and competition from college and the Panthers cap fandom and opportunity. Retail leans on malls and outlets, with few tastemaker doors.

headline: Six banners sell themselves. Nike's job is the cold walk to 1901 W. Madison.

archetype.name: The Six-Banner Congregation
archetype.description: A multigenerational faith in the 1991-98 Bulls that spans every side of town. It keeps buying through losing seasons but meets every rebuild promise with South Side and West Side sarcasm. The banners and the red-and-black have its loyalty. The roster has to earn it.

pulse.teamMoment: Year one of a new regime. Billy Donovan stepped down, Tiago Splitter took over as coach, and EVP Bryson Graham is building a size-first 'SLAP' roster. The core is Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis and No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson, with Norman Powell and Nic Claxton added. The Bulls are coming off 31-51, sit low in power rankings and have no opening-night or Christmas Day game. Their early national stage is Emirates NBA Cup East Group C, against Boston, Atlanta, Charlotte and Washington.
pulse.sentiment: Guarded hope under ownership fatigue. Fans like the draft and Wilson's First Team All-Summer League debut, but they've learned to mock hype and wait for proof.

verifiedMoment: New regime. Billy Donovan stepped down and Tiago Splitter took over as coach. New EVP Bryson Graham is building for 'SLAP' (size, length, athleticism, physicality) around Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis and No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson.

scorecard.rationale: The six-banner heritage engine and a full flagship-to-mall network put Chicago second in the league on retail and top five on culture. A 31-51 rebuild and a 2027-28 build window hold opportunity and fandom nearer the middle (brief scores: opportunity 82, culture 93, retail 84, fandom 74). Chicago has one of the league's deepest design cultures, and it's a global heritage retail engine with a full network of flagship, arena, boutiques and suburban malls. Fan intensity scores high on legacy but is held back by a 31-51 rebuild and ownership fatigue. Near-term upside is in civic and outerwear product, mostly in the 2027-28 cycle, more than in current-player demand.

headline: The jersey says Cleveland. The street says The Land.

archetype.name: The 3-1 Believer
archetype.description: This fan keeps score in Cleveland scars: The Drive, The Fumble, The Shot. There's one release, the 2016 comeback from 3-1 down that ended a 52-year drought in a Game 7. They still call the arena the Q. Last spring's 125-94 Game 7 rout of No. 1 Detroit was fun for exactly one series, until the Knicks sweep. So they buy what has happened, not what's promised, and say 216 or 330 before any slogan.

pulse.teamMoment: Cleveland went 52-30, won two Game 7s (one a 125-94 rout of No. 1 Detroit) and got swept in the East Finals by the eventual champion Knicks. Then it went all in: Mitchell extended, Harden re-signed and the last tradable first spent on Peyton Watson. It's title or bust, with no opening-night or Christmas Day game.
pulse.sentiment: Optimistic and impatient. The playoff run made believers, but the Knicks sweep, thinner depth (Wade, Ellis and Nance are gone) and a scout's public doubt keep title talk guarded.

verifiedMoment: All in. The Cavs reached their first conference finals since 2018. Then they re-signed James Harden, extended Donovan Mitchell and spent their last tradable first on Peyton Watson. It's title or bust.

scorecard.rationale: Title-or-bust loyalty puts fandom above average. Cleveland's punk, rap, steel and Akron material sits below the league median. A drive-to-the-mall retail map with no sneaker district and a Browns-first fall keep retail below the line and opportunity at it (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 76, retail 48, fandom 72). Cleveland has deep, designable local culture: punk and rap lineage, ore-dock steel and Deco civic stone, immigrant food rituals and a distinct Akron identity. Its regional fan base is loyal and title-hungry. The near-term upside is capped, though. Retail is a drive-to-the-mall map with no downtown sneaker district, and the fall wallet is Browns-first. There's only one national home date (MLK Day), and the LeBron storyline is one Nike must handle carefully.

headline: Detroit wears the city first and the Pistons second, so build with its makers and talk like a shift.

archetype.name: The Blue-Collar Contender
archetype.description: A fan base that defines itself by effort, defense and being counted out, now holding a 60-win team it doesn't fully trust yet. It rewards grit and local credit. It punishes gloss, hype and outsider 'comeback city' pity.

pulse.teamMoment: Detroit went 60-22 as the East's No. 1 seed, then lost 4-3 to Cleveland in the second round, capped by a 125-94 Game 7. The core stayed: Jalen Duren re-signed for 5 years and $200M, and Isaiah Stewart was traded to Memphis. In came John Collins, Isaiah Joe, Taurean Prince, Gary Harris and rookie Ebuka Okorie, all under J.B. Bickerstaff. The season opens Oct 20 at home to Boston on NBC. There's no Christmas Day game.
pulse.sentiment: Proud but nervous. Cade Cunningham's All-NBA First Team year and Duren's deal feel earned. But the Game 7 blowout is still raw, and fans and analysts doubt there's a second creator beside Cade.

verifiedMoment: A 60-win, No. 1-seed season ended in a Game 7 blowout by Cleveland. Detroit kept its core anyway, signing Jalen Duren for $200M. The open question: does Cade Cunningham have enough help without a second star?

scorecard.rationale: A 60-win No. 1 seed in a Specter year, a seven-month outerwear season and a deep maker culture lift opportunity, culture and fandom well above average. A thin city-core retail map and unconfirmed partner doors keep retail below the line (brief scores: opportunity 80, culture 90, retail 55, fandom 80). A 60-win No. 1 seed in a Specter year, three heritage wardrobes and a seven-month outerwear season put opportunity well above average. In our judgment, Detroit's design well is unusually deep: Motown, techno, jit, Dilla, Pewabic, Deco, workwear, immigrant corridors. Retail scores cautiously because the city core is thin and main partner doors are unconfirmed (Detroit vs. Everybody, Two18, Nike Factory at Great Lakes Crossing). Fandom is intense, but it shares winter with the Lions and Red Wings and is anxious after the Game 7 rout.

headline: Indiana is where the game lives, and this season the NBA brings its Cup final to Hinkle.

archetype.name: The Keepers of the Gym
archetype.description: Fans raised on a single-class state tournament that ran until 1997, on county gyms that out-seat their towns and on Hinkle's 1928 barrel vault. They reward effort over flash, and their navy and gold is Pacers loyalty that travels from Mass Ave to New Castle.

pulse.teamMoment: Tyrese Haliburton is back from the Achilles tear he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals. After a 19-63 season, he rejoins Siakam, Nembhard, Nesmith, McConnell and deadline pickup Ivica Zubac under Rick Carlisle. Kelly Oubre Jr., Larry Nance Jr. and two-way Purdue guard Braden Smith join them. Indiana hosts the 76ers on the Oct 30 opening Cup Night and has no opening-night or Christmas Day game.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously hopeful and protective. Fans expect a bounce-back toward contention, but they remember how fast the 2025 high ended. They will punish anything that feels like hype or exploits the injury.

verifiedMoment: Tyrese Haliburton is back from the torn Achilles he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals. 'I am healthy, ready to go,' he said Sept 28. After a lost 19-63 year, he rejoins the Siakam-led 2025 Finals core, with Ivica Zubac now at center.

scorecard.rationale: A Hinkle Cup final and Haliburton's return give a small market near-average opportunity and above-average gym-faith fandom. Value-led, mall-first retail with no destination door sits in the bottom tier (brief scores: opportunity 68, culture 76, retail 45, fandom 72). Indiana has one of the league's deepest basketball cultures and a one-off Hinkle Cup final in a comeback season. That lifts opportunity above average despite a small market. Retail sits below average: no destination flagship, a mall-first, value-led buyer, a star with a rival footwear deal and major cues that need third-party clearance.

headline: Giannis joins Heat Culture: win Miami court by court and barrio by barrio, in three languages.

archetype.name: The Title-or-Bust Diaspora
archetype.description: A multinational, trilingual crowd that judges the Heat on effort and playoff nights, and dresses for the arena like it's dinner or the club. With a Giannis-Bam contender, it now expects a championship.

pulse.teamMoment: Miami went 43-39 as the No. 10 seed and lost a 127-126 overtime Play-In at Charlotte. Then it traded Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware and a haul of picks for Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis, and signed Klay Thompson. Under Erik Spoelstra, a Giannis-Bam Adebayo frontcourt makes 2026-27 title-or-bust.
pulse.sentiment: Euphoric and demanding. The mood flipped from Play-In frustration to championship expectations, with real worry about depth after losing Herro, Jaquez, Ware and Norman Powell. ESPN openly doubts the supporting cast.

verifiedMoment: Miami landed Giannis Antetokounmpo in one of the biggest trades in NBA history, then added Klay Thompson. On paper it's a Giannis-Bam Adebayo contender. Anything short of a deep run will read as failure.

scorecard.rationale: Top-three opportunity: Giannis is Nike's biggest signature star, in a gateway shopping market with deep Cuban, Haitian and Latin design material. Fandom is just above average because Miami's crowd runs on playoffs and winning, not lifelong loyalty (brief scores: opportunity 86, culture 92, retail 78, fandom 72). A Nike signature superstar is arriving in a gateway shopping market. Add some of the league's deepest multicultural design material and a real park-court culture, and opportunity and culture rank near the top of the league. Retail is strong but sprawling and pressured by knockoffs. Fandom peaks on White Hot playoff nights, but it's more front-running than in the league's most loyal markets.

headline: With Giannis gone, the Bucks belong to Cream City again: sell the brick and the cold, not a new star.

archetype.name: The Working-City Loyalist
archetype.description: A statewide, blue-collar fan base that expects to be overlooked and values effort over glamour. It stays loyal through a rebuild, but punishes anything that talks down to it or cashes in on its grief.

pulse.teamMoment: Milwaukee opens 2026-27 rebuilding, coming off a 32-50 season and the trade that sent Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to Miami. Taylor Jenkins is the new coach. The core is Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware, Myles Turner, Kyle Kuzma and rookie Brayden Burries.
pulse.sentiment: Grief and some anger over the trade, resignation about a long rebuild and cautious curiosity about Herro and the rookies. Nostalgia for 2021 is the safest emotion. Everyone has Jan 28 circled.

verifiedMoment: For the first time in more than a decade, Milwaukee starts a season without Giannis Antetokounmpo. New coach Taylor Jenkins leads a long rebuild around Tyler Herro, the young pieces from the Miami trade and two lottery picks.

scorecard.rationale: Life after Giannis in a small, value-minded rebuild gives Milwaukee the league's second-lowest opportunity. Cream City brick and fish-fry Fridays are its main design assets, and fandom stays below average until Jan 28 (brief scores: opportunity 50, culture 70, retail 40, fandom 56). Milwaukee has one of the league's most place-specific palettes and a deep tavern and neighborhood vernacular. But it's a small, value-minded market in a low-expectation rebuild, with a thin sneaker scene and no Nike-owned door in the city. That keeps opportunity average and retail below average, which is why the plan runs only three priority-1 bets. Fandom is loyal and statewide, but at low heat until Jan 28.

headline: New York waited 53 years for this ring. Sell it through parks, counters and borough doors, not the skyline.

archetype.name: The Vindicated Lifers
archetype.description: A multigenerational, five-borough fan base that kept selling out the Mecca through 53 ringless years and now wants to say 'told you' in its own codes. It prizes grit, defense and heritage over flash, and spots anything corporate or touristy from a block away.

pulse.teamMoment: Defending champions. The Knicks went 53-29, then 16-3 in the playoffs, closing out San Antonio 94-90 in Game 5 with Brunson as Finals MVP. The core is intact under the second apron. The defense opens with ring night on Oct 20 against LeBron James' and Jaylen Brown's 76ers.
pulse.sentiment: Euphoric and protective. Fans are flush with the first title since 1973 and expect a real defense in a tougher East. Old grievances with ownership are quieter, not forgotten.

verifiedMoment: The champs. The Knicks won their first title since 1973, with Jalen Brunson as Finals MVP, and kept most of the roster under the second apron. The title defense opens with ring night against LeBron James and Jaylen Brown's new-look 76ers.

scorecard.rationale: The league ceiling on opportunity, culture and fandom: the biggest market, defending its first title since 1973, with the deepest homegrown basketball, music and art culture. Retail sits just behind the Lakers and Chicago because MSG, Puma's Clyde and Fanatics crowd Nike's lane in the most license-heavy market (brief scores: opportunity 91, culture 96, retail 84, fandom 94). The league's biggest market is defending its first title in 53 years, with the deepest homegrown basketball, music and art culture to design from. Crowding holds the scores down: this is the most license-heavy market, with MSG, MTA, Puma's Clyde, Fanatics and a 2026-27 City Edition that is unverified and likely already set. Nike's real lanes are the AF1 Uptowns and Flax, Specter, the park circuit and the borough doors, all assuming rights and doors check out.

headline: Win the 407, not the postcard: in a city of arrivals, the Magic are the one shared flag.

archetype.name: The Transplant City's Flag
archetype.description: A fan base of arrivals: Northeast transplants, Boricua families, Haitian and Jamaican Pine Hills, park workers and Gen Z Banchero kids. They share little but the Magic and the 407. They're loyal to 'our guys', nostalgic for Penny's pinstripes and allergic to being taken for tourists, especially when visiting fans fill Kia Center.

pulse.teamMoment: Orlando chose continuity. Jamahl Mosley was fired after a 45-37 season that ended in a Play-In escape and a first-round loss to No. 1 Detroit. Sean Sweeney arrived from San Antonio, and Vucevic is back beside Banchero, Wagner and Bane. The open questions: Wagner's health after 34 games, and three ball-dominant stars with no true point guard.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously hopeful but impatient. Fans like the core and Vucevic's return, but the mood has moved from 'rebuild' to 'prove it'. Nobody wants hype before results.

verifiedMoment: Orlando picked continuity over a splash. It fired Jamahl Mosley and hired Sean Sweeney, the Spurs' defensive architect, betting he can make the Banchero-Wagner-Bane trio work. Nikola Vucevic is back for a second Magic stint.

scorecard.rationale: Penny pinstripes and a large Boricua base give Orlando a real lane, with design material below the median. No national stage, outlet-heavy retail and playoff-gated loyalty keep opportunity, retail and fandom in the bottom half (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 72, retail 58, fandom 56). Opportunity sits above average: Nike owns the Penny-pinstripe nostalgia, and Central Florida's Puerto Rican and tourist audiences are large. No national-TV stage, modest local incomes and a prove-it season cap it. Culture runs deep (Parramore, OBT signage, Mills 50, Boricua Orlando), though the score assumes partners the brief hasn't signed yet. Retail is outlet-heavy with a thin taste layer, and fandom is loyal but playoff-gated.

headline: Philly loves a Sixer who earns it. Build from the gym, the order counter and Broad Street, not 1776.

archetype.name: The Prove-It Family
archetype.description: Suspicious by default, ride-or-die once a player bleeds for the city. Booing is accountability, and out-of-town grinders like Iverson and Kelce get adopted for life.

pulse.teamMoment: After a 45-37 Play-In season, Philly came back from 3-1 down against No. 2 Boston, then got swept in the second round by the eventual champion Knicks. Philly then traded Paul George for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join Embiid, Maxey and Edgecombe. Title odds moved to about +1000, and Nick Nurse is under maximum pressure.
pulse.sentiment: Giddy but braced. The city knows three things decide the year: Embiid's availability, LeBron turning 42 in December and the fresh Knicks wound. It will judge both new stars on effort, not reputation.

verifiedMoment: The summer's biggest swing. Jaylen Brown arrived by trade from Boston, and LeBron James signed as a free agent to join Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe. Health and age are the questions, and Nick Nurse is under maximum pressure.

scorecard.rationale: A LeBron-and-Brown contender in a Specter year gives Philadelphia top-four opportunity and near-elite fandom. Its design material (Philly soul, the mural program, North Fifth Street, Iverson-era street style) is real but less distinct than the top culture band. Thin taste-setting independents and a throwback lane owned by Mitchell & Ness hold retail down (brief scores: opportunity 86, culture 91, retail 68, fandom 85). A title-contending superteam with Nike's LeBron, a Specter season and a new arena coming to the Spectrum site make this one of the league's biggest 2026-27 openings. Few markets offer as deep a culture to design from. Retail is broad, but the taste-setting independents are thin since Ubiq closed, and the throwback lane belongs to Mitchell & Ness. Fan intensity is elite but shares the winter with the Eagles.

headline: Canada's only NBA team lives by borough and dresses for winter. Let Toronto co-author the Kawhi reunion.

archetype.name: The Defiant North
archetype.description: A diaspora-built, country-sized fanbase that turned being overlooked into identity. It cheers loud, expects heartbreak and rewards brands that let it tell its own story.

pulse.teamMoment: Kawhi Leonard is back from the Clippers (final year, $50.3M) to pair with All-Star Scottie Barnes. Last season went 46-36 as the 5 seed and ended in a 4-3 first-round loss to Cleveland. Darko Rajakovic is extended through 2028-29.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously excited about a real push toward the East's upper tier. The shadows are the 35-year-old Leonard's health and the unprotected 2031 and 2033 firsts that left with Ingram and Dick.

verifiedMoment: Kawhi Leonard is back in Toronto. After a surprise 5-seed season, the Raptors got him from the Clippers to pair with All-Star Scottie Barnes. Coach Darko Rajakovic is newly extended through 2028-29.

scorecard.rationale: A country-sized market with the Leonard reunion and Nike's own Carter archive sits above average everywhere. CAD pricing, cross-border leakage and post-'Elbows Up' wariness of US brands hold it below the US giants (brief scores: opportunity 78, culture 88, retail 70, fandom 80). Culture and fandom score well above average. The fanbase is country-sized and diaspora-majority, the 2019 memory is open again, the Leonard jersey is spiking and Nike owns the Carter archive. The design vocabulary runs unusually deep: transit, winter, borough, heritage. Retail is strong in malls and national chains but held back by CAD pricing, cross-border and resale leakage, and the anti-US mood.

headline: Sell the District, not 'Washington': the flag, the wards and paid go-go partners make the Dybantsa era DC's to wear.

archetype.name: The Hometown Behind the Capital
archetype.description: A Black-built, DMV-wide fan base, loyal to the District and the 1978 banner more than to the modern Wizards, that wears DC civic symbols as identity. It commits when the team speaks DC and shows up East of the River, not on the Mall.

pulse.teamMoment: Washington went from the NBA's worst record (17-65) to winning the lottery. No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa joins Trae Young (re-signed for about $212M over four years) and Anthony Davis. Under Brian Keefe, the young core is Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George and Tre Johnson. There's no opening-night or Christmas game. The first confirmed home date of note is the Oct 30 Cup Night against Charlotte in East Group C, a regional stage, not a national one.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously curious: real excitement about Dybantsa and the Young-Davis pairing, wrapped in gallows humor. It's a show-me crowd that wants proof on health and fit before it fully commits.

verifiedMoment: From the NBA's worst record to one of its most interesting builds. Lottery winner AJ Dybantsa joins Trae Young, re-signed long term, and Anthony Davis. Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George and Tre Johnson round out the young core.

scorecard.rationale: DC's go-go, flag and ward culture sits in the league's top third. A 17-65 hangover in a hockey-first, visiting-fan-heavy arena gives it the fourth-softest fandom until Dybantsa proves out (brief scores: opportunity 66, culture 90, retail 58, fandom 44). DC has one of the league's deepest, most ownable local cultures: an official music, a beloved civic flag and type system, Chocolate City and DMV hoops. The Dybantsa reset makes this an above-average opening. Fandom sits below average after 17-65, in a hockey-first arena heavy with visiting fans. Retail is a wealthy but fragmented suburban market of malls and DTLR. So the plan holds to three priorities, with gates.

headline: Dallas taste is set in Oak Cliff, Deep Ellum and Fair Park. Win there first, then sell north.

archetype.name: The Wounded Loyalists
archetype.description: A sprawling, multicultural metroplex crowd that still measures everything against Dirk and 2011. Guarded since the Luka trade, it will trust Flagg, and spend its kids' money on him, if the product feels like Dallas rather than generic Texas.

pulse.teamMoment: A full reset under new president Masai Ujiri and first-year coach Dusty May, built around Cooper Flagg. Kyrie Irving is back from his ACL tear, joined by Zaccharie Risacher, Santi Aldama and No. 9 pick Morez Johnson Jr. BetMGM sets the win total at 34.5, and the playoffs look unlikely.
pulse.sentiment: Cautious optimism. The 'Fire Nico' anger has burned out now that Harrison is gone and the Davis trade is done. Fans are still processing the Luka trade and a 26-56 season, and they'll reward visible development over hype.

verifiedMoment: A full reset. New president Masai Ujiri and first-year coach Dusty May build around Cooper Flagg, with Kyrie Irving back from his ACL tear.

scorecard.rationale: A huge metro with Flagg and distinct Oak Cliff and Fair Park languages has average retail scale and design material below the median. A wounded 26-56 fan base and football's grip on the fall put opportunity and fandom in the bottom half (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 70, retail 58, fandom 54). A huge, majority-minority metro with distinct design languages (the Fair Park Centennial, Deep Ellum, Oak Cliff) and a fresh Flagg reason to buy. Holding it back: football's grip on the fall, a car-bound retail map, a wounded fan base coming off 26-56 and partners not yet confirmed.

headline: Denver fans want layers that beat the weather and a skyline nobody redraws.

archetype.name: The Mile High Loyalists
archetype.description: A patient, statewide base that waited decades for the 2023 title. Now it guards its own symbols (Jokic, the rainbow skyline, the altitude) against hype, bandwagons and anything corporate.

pulse.teamMoment: A 54-28 season ended in a 4-2 first-round upset by sixth-seeded Minnesota. Denver is betting on continuity around three-time MVP Nikola Jokic under coach David Adelman. It added 37-year-old DeMar DeRozan on a one-year deal. With a 49.5 win total, it sits in the second tier of contenders behind OKC and San Antonio.
pulse.sentiment: Loyal but anxious. Fans are proud of the title and Jokic, and impatient with the bench after a second playoff exit to Minnesota in three seasons. Their hopes rest on Jokic signing his roughly $290M extension and on the DeRozan fit.

verifiedMoment: Denver is betting on continuity around three-time MVP Nikola Jokic after a first-round upset. DeMar DeRozan arrives for scoring. Jokic is eligible for an extension of roughly $290M and has said he aims to sign it.

scorecard.rationale: A three-time MVP, a 49.5-win total and a long outerwear season keep opportunity close to the pack. A quiet, understated base, an edge-of-metro retail map and a narrower design well than most put Denver just below average (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 68, retail 48, fandom 64). A three-time MVP, a recent title, one of the league's most loved vintage graphics and a long outerwear season give Denver above-average opportunity and deep design material. Retail is below average: no downtown Nike door, a thin sneaker-boutique scene, and volume on the suburban edges. Fandom is loyal but quiet until the playoffs.

headline: Oakland is the soul, San Francisco the address. Win the Bay from the bridge between them, dressed for fog.

archetype.name: The Dynasty Diaspora
archetype.description: Forged in 40 lean Oakland years and spoiled by four titles, this fan base now spreads across The Town, The City and the 408. It's loyal to Curry, Draymond and Kerr more than to any arena, and it misses Oracle in a building that never had Oracle's soul.

pulse.teamMoment: Curry's aging core ran it back. Last season ended at 37-45, with a play-in win over the Clippers and a 111-96 loss at Phoenix. The Warriors chased Giannis and Anthony Davis without landing a deal. They re-signed Porzingis, Horford, Melton and Gary Payton II, added Niang and Brandon Williams, and drafted Yaxel Lendeborg at No. 11. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are recovering from injury.
pulse.sentiment: Grateful and anxious. Fans are invested in the dynasty-era window but expect little: the win total is 40.5, and previews doubt a play-in spot. That mood favors keepsake and heritage buying over hype.

verifiedMoment: Stephen Curry's aging core runs it back. The Warriors explored Giannis and Anthony Davis but couldn't land another star. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are still recovering from injuries.

scorecard.rationale: Oakland, San Francisco and Asian American lineages put the Bay's design well in the league's top band, and its spending keeps retail high. A 40.5-win total and an open Curry shoe deal hold opportunity and fandom at the league middle (brief scores: opportunity 72, culture 92, retail 78, fandom 70). Culture scores near the top: two cities, three subcultural lineages and huge Asian American communities. Opportunity sits in the low 70s, held down by a 40.5 win total, injured Butler and Moody, an open Curry deal and a winter-only window. A Curry-Nike deal, confirmed Specter game dates and a hot November would push it back toward 80.

headline: In Houston the finish is the flex: sell candy paint and Clutch City red and gold, not a logo.

archetype.name: The Overlooked Originators
archetype.description: A hyper-diverse, Black and brown metro that invented slab, screw and Clutch City, and still feels underrated next to Dallas and the coasts. It rewards brands that credit the source and punishes ones that borrow the look.

pulse.teamMoment: Houston went 52-30, then lost 4-2 to the Lakers in the first round. The team kept Ime Udoka and the Durant-Sengun core. Amen Thompson got an extension of 5 years and $208M, Tari Eason 5 years and $81.5M. Marcus Smart, Bogdan Bogdanovic and shooting coach Chip Engelland arrived. BetMGM sets the win total at 47.5.
pulse.sentiment: Judgment call, not measured: hopeful but impatient after a first-round exit. A 47.5 win total and summer Durant trade chatter keep expectations flatter than last year's 52 wins.

verifiedMoment: After a first-round exit, Houston kept Ime Udoka and the Kevin Durant-Alperen Sengun core. It locked up Amen Thompson and Tari Eason, then added veterans Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic.

scorecard.rationale: One of the league's most complete local design languages and a Durant-Sengun playoff team keep culture high and opportunity above average. Car-bound sprawl and an attention war with football, the Astros and the rodeo keep retail near average and fandom below it (brief scores: opportunity 76, culture 90, retail 62, fandom 64). Houston has one of the league's deepest, most specific design wells: slab, grillz, Black cowboy style, a full basketball lineage and the country's most diverse neighborhoods. It also has a 52-win team with Durant and a newly extended young core. But retail is big, car-dependent and spread thin. The 47.5 win total points to a flatter year, and the Rockets fight football, the Astros and the rodeo for attention.

headline: No star, no Christmas game, owner suspended: the Clippers' best asset is their Inglewood address.

archetype.name: The New Homeowners
archetype.description: A chip-on-the-shoulder minority that waited out Buffalo, San Diego, the Sterling years and two decades as the downtown tenant. Now it defines itself by the house in Inglewood and the blocks around it, not by banners or stars.

pulse.teamMoment: A post-Kawhi reset under Tyronn Lue, built around Darius Garland, Brandon Ingram and No. 5 pick Keaton Wagler. Last season went 42-40 and ended in a 126-121 play-in loss to Golden State. Meanwhile, the NBA's Sept 2 Aspiration ruling suspends Steve Ballmer for a year, fines the team $30M and strips its 2029-2033 first-round picks.
pulse.sentiment: Bruised and defensive. Diehards rally around the team's 'witch hunt' framing and an us-against-the-league mood. Casual LA fans are drifting to the Lakers, Dodgers and Rams, and closets full of Kawhi jerseys have nowhere to go.

verifiedMoment: A post-Kawhi reset around Darius Garland, Brandon Ingram and No. 5 pick Keaton Wagler. The NBA's Aspiration penalties hang over it all: Steve Ballmer is suspended for a year, and the team forfeits five first-round picks.

scorecard.rationale: The Inglewood-to-SGV footprint gives the Clippers real design material, if below the league median, and LA retail keeps retail above average. A starless post-Kawhi reset in the Lakers' shadow means the league's third-thinnest fandom and a low opportunity score that holds with or without the Aspiration penalties (brief scores: opportunity 60, culture 80, retail 72, fandom 41). Calibrated to a league average of 50. The footprint (Inglewood, South and Southeast LA, Long Beach, the SGV, Little Saigon, the IE) gives real design material, and LA retail runs every tier. But Nike doors are thin near Inglewood, launch lead times are short and the Lakers own the volume. Fandom sits among the league's thinnest: a small, loyal, bruised base with no star, no national stage and an owner suspended. The scores hold with or without the penalties.

archetype.name: The Inherited Dynasty
archetype.description: Handed purple and gold by a parent or a block, these fans judge every new star by one test: does he belong in the line from Magic to Kobe? The throwback of their era is a family crest, and newcomers have to earn the 8/24 shrine's respect.

pulse.teamMoment: The full Luka Doncic era begins now that LeBron James has left for Philadelphia. Reaves is max-extended and Walker Kessler arrived at center. None of the top five playoff-minutes players returned from the 53-29 team that OKC swept in the West semifinals. BetMGM sets the win total at 46.5, sixth in the West. JJ Redick, in his third season, says the fit is better.
pulse.sentiment: Cautious excitement, shot through with grief. Fans are curious about a Doncic-Reaves-Kessler core and feel real loss as the LeBron era ends, hardest in Black LA, which also carried the Kobe and Showtime eras. The emotional Dec 25 return is already circled.

verifiedMoment: The full Luka Doncic era starts now that LeBron James has left for Philadelphia. The Lakers built around Doncic, max-extended Austin Reaves and put Walker Kessler at center. None of their top five players in playoff minutes returned, a first in NBA history.

scorecard.rationale: Second only to New York on opportunity and first on retail: a reset jersey wall in the league's most mythologized brand meets every retail tier. Fandom sits below the true elite this season, on grief over LeBron and a 46.5-win projection (brief scores: opportunity 90, culture 94, retail 88, fandom 86). The NBA's most mythologized brand is resetting its jersey wall in a vast, multilingual market. Few cities can match its design traditions: South Central signage, Chicano lettering and serigraphs, lowriders, Kobe murals and immigrant food color. Every retail tier, from Fairfax to Citadel, is already there. Fandom sits a notch lower this season because grief over LeBron and a 46.5-win projection temper the heat.

headline: Memphis is between stars, so sell the city: the 901, Penny and paid local hands.

archetype.name: The Grindhouse Family
archetype.description: Fans who love the Grizzlies as the face of an underestimated city. They measure every new player against Z-Bo, Tony Allen and Marc Gasol, and they stay through lean years as long as the effort and the respect for Memphis are real.

pulse.teamMoment: A full reset. Ja Morant and Jaren Jackson Jr. are gone, and No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer leads a young core with Zach Edey and Cedric Coward under Tuomas Iisalo. After a 25-57 season, this is likely a lottery team, playing in NBA Cup West Group B.
pulse.sentiment: Bruised but curious. Fans are still processing the Morant breakup and want effort, honesty and a reason to adopt Boozer. Edey's health is the nightly worry.

verifiedMoment: A full reset. Ja Morant and Jaren Jackson Jr. are gone, and No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer leads a young core with Zach Edey and Cedric Coward.

scorecard.rationale: Memphis's design well (soul, living rap, jookin, sign painting) is in the league's top third. A post-Ja reset in a small, price-conscious metro with no Nike door puts retail second from the bottom (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 88, retail 38, fandom 66). Memphis has one of the league's deepest and most ownable design wells: soul, living rap, jookin, civil rights memory, sign-painted lettering and dry-rub barbecue. Its fan base is fiercely loyal. But a rebuild year, a small, price-conscious metro and no confirmed Nike-owned door cap retail readiness, so every priority-1 line carries a Nov 30 stop-loss. The opportunity is real because Penny and a city-first story can sell without a star.

headline: In Minnesota, Nike wins on the skyway walk: warm layers, the North Star and community-led product, not the stars' shoes.

archetype.name: The Patient North
archetype.description: A polite, stubborn statewide fan base that wears its scars: Garnett's exit, the drought, a West semifinal exit to San Antonio. It wants belief, not victory laps. It dresses for wind chill below zero and reps area codes and neighborhoods before skylines.

pulse.teamMoment: After a 49-33 season, a first-round upset of Denver and a West semifinal loss to San Antonio, Minnesota went all in on Anthony Edwards by trading for LaMelo Ball. The Wolves have 27 national TV games, host OKC on Christmas and carry a 48.5-win total. Under Chris Finch, they have title aspirations.
pulse.sentiment: Optimistic and impatient. Fans are thrilled by the Edwards-Ball backcourt but still sore about the price: Naz Reid, Julius Randle and a pile of picks. The Knicks, who host the Wolves on MLK Day, won the 2026 title, and that adds an edge.

verifiedMoment: Minnesota went all in on Anthony Edwards, trading for LaMelo Ball to build one of the league's most electric backcourts. The Wolves have 27 national TV games and host OKC on Christmas.

scorecard.rationale: A loud Edwards-Ball team with a Christmas home game, Garnett's retirement and a deep Minneapolis Sound, Mill City and Somali, Hmong and Native design well put opportunity, culture and fandom above average. Both stars wear rival brands, though, and retail is led by suburban malls (brief scores: opportunity 72, culture 84, retail 58, fandom 76). Minnesota has one of the league's deepest design vernaculars: the Minneapolis Sound, Mill City, winter craft and strong Somali, Hmong, Native and Northside scenes. It also has a newly loud Edwards-Ball fan base. Retail is suburban and mall-led with few taste doors, and both stars' rival shoe deals cap Nike's athlete-led upside.

headline: Sell New Orleans first and the Pelicans second: paid, hand-made craft on the city's own clock.

archetype.name: The Second Line
archetype.description: They dance behind the city's main line of Saints, LSU and Carnival. They stayed loyal through two lost franchises and get loud when the music is right. They buy city pride first and team gear second, and they punish anything that reads tourist.

pulse.teamMoment: New coach Jamahl Mosley inherits a 26-56 team after a quiet offseason under Joe Dumars. He gets Zion Williamson, breakout scorer Trey Murphy III (21.5 ppg, kept through June trade rumors) and second-years Derik Queen and Jeremiah Fears. The Pelicans aren't on the opening-night or Christmas slates. Their early-season stage is NBA Cup West Group B (OKC, MIN, LAC, MEM), which opens Oct 30 at the Clippers.
pulse.sentiment: Weary, not angry. Fans are protective of Murphy, hopeful on Queen and Fears, and cautious about building anything on Zion's availability. The "NOLA Nights" Skelican City Edition excites them more than the roster does. It came back in 2025-26, though the 2026-27 design is unverified.

verifiedMoment: New coach Jamahl Mosley inherits Zion Williamson, breakout Trey Murphy III and youngsters Derik Queen and Jeremiah Fears. The offseason was quiet, with no first-round pick.

scorecard.rationale: The starkest split in the league: New Orleans's culture is second only to New York's, but thin retail, a Saints-first city and a 26-56 team put opportunity, retail and fandom at the floor. It's a craft market, not a volume market (brief scores: opportunity 46, culture 96, retail 34, fandom 38). Few NBA cities have a deeper or more design-ready local culture, and its calendar lines up with the season. But retail is thin: few destination sneaker doors, a modest arena store and a price-conscious core. Pelicans fandom is small, Saints-first and weary after 26-56. The opportunity sits just below average, held up by city-first product that can sell regardless of the standings.

headline: Oklahoma has one big-league team. Dress the whole state in Thunder blue, under $100.

archetype.name: The One-Team State
archetype.description: A whole state that adopted a franchise in 2008 and now wears a champion as its civic uniform. Loud, loyal, value-minded and allergic to flash the team has not earned.

pulse.teamMoment: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is a back-to-back MVP, and his Thunder went 64-18 before San Antonio beat them 4-3 in the West finals. They're 2026-27 co-title favorites, with a BetMGM win total of 60.5, the West's highest. Luguentz Dort went to Atlanta, and Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins were traded too. In came draft picks Aday Mara (No. 12), Bennett Stirtz and Otega Oweh. Presti is keeping a payroll near $260M rather than cutting it.
pulse.sentiment: Confident but stung. Fans expect a title and see the Oct 20 opener at San Antonio as a grudge match. They trust Presti and Mark Daigneault's patient build, even as familiar rotation players leave.

verifiedMoment: Back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Thunder are 2026-27 title co-favorites. San Antonio ended their title defense in a seven-game West finals. Payroll is rising toward about $260M, and Sam Presti says he won't cut to avoid it.

scorecard.rationale: The league's second-most intense fandom and a 60.5-win co-favorite with a Converse-signed star put opportunity in the top ten, scored on demand and Nike's rights position, not doors. Small-metro, value-minded retail and a thinner design well than the culture capitals keep retail and culture below average (brief scores: opportunity 70, culture 66, retail 40, fandom 86). A champion that's the only big-league team in a whole state gives OKC near-top fan intensity and a big statewide opportunity for a small metro. Red dirt, Skydance, Route 66 and community stories give designers plenty to work from. Retail lags: it's a car-based, value-minded market with no Nike community door and a small sneaker scene.

headline: All-Star comes home. Design Phoenix from the street up, not from another sunset.

archetype.name: The Sun-Faded Faithful
archetype.description: A Valley of transplants and barrio families who adopted a team that has never won a title. They show it in thrifted, UV-bleached purple and orange, not banners. The pride is in having stayed through 1976, 1993 and 2021, and in surviving the heat.

pulse.teamMoment: The Suns went 45-37 last year and were swept 4-0 by OKC. Since then the Booker-Jalen Green team has re-signed Brooks, Gillespie, Mark Williams and Goodwin, and added Miles Bridges, Luke Kennard and Koa Peat under Jordan Ott. A 40.5 win total puts them on the play-in bubble.
pulse.sentiment: Guarded and pragmatic. Fans are tired after the superteam collapse, glad the club kept its own and loyal to Booker. Hosting All-Star excites them more than the standings.

verifiedMoment: The Devin Booker-Jalen Green Suns kept their own and added Miles Bridges. They re-signed Brooks, Gillespie, Mark Williams and Goodwin, aiming to climb out of the West's middle tier.

scorecard.rationale: Hosting All-Star (Feb 19-21) and an under-served Latino base lift opportunity above average. The Valley's Chicano, Indigenous and Van Buren neon material puts culture just below the league median. Retail is around average, and a bubble roster holds fandom below it (brief scores: opportunity 78, culture 82, retail 62, fandom 64). A home All-Star Weekend, a large, youth-heavy Latino base the assortment under-serves and an unused street-level look push opportunity and culture well above average. A short licensing clock this season tempers that. Retail is sprawling and mall-led, with few taste doors. Fandom is loyal but shaped by a bubble roster and no title.

headline: The '77 title turns 50 in Nike's hometown. Build it for the Big Dark, with Albina.

archetype.name: The Insider Loyalist
archetype.description: A fan base that stayed through 814 sellouts, the Jail Blazers and Lillard's exit and return. It lives next door to Beaverton, so it reads every jersey for fabric, fit and who designed it. It wants its story told from inside the city, never as a Portlandia punchline.

pulse.teamMoment: New owner Tom Dundon's Blazers add Ja Morant, acquired from Memphis on June 29, to a backcourt with Damian Lillard, back from a torn Achilles. Micah Nori is the first-year coach. Last season went 42-40 and ended 4-1 to San Antonio in the first round. Oregon, Multnomah County and Portland have committed $586M to Moda Center upgrades, but the lease is still unsigned.
pulse.sentiment: Hopeful but guarded. Fans are emotional about Lillard back in a Blazers uniform after a lost season, and split on Morant's talent versus his 2023 suspensions. They debate whether Nori brings one of them off the bench. They're relieved the team is staying, and wary of an owner who says he won't pay for the renovation.

verifiedMoment: New owner Tom Dundon's Blazers pair Ja Morant with Damian Lillard, back from a torn Achilles, under first-year coach Micah Nori. The Moda Center renovation lease is still being negotiated.

scorecard.rationale: Nike's hometown, a once-only '77-at-50 year, a Lillard-Morant backcourt and intense statewide loyalty lift opportunity and fandom well above average. Few public Nike doors and a Rose Quarter retail desert put retail below it (brief scores: opportunity 76, culture 84, retail 56, fandom 80). A once-only heritage year, an empty City Edition slot and a deep roster in Nike's own hometown make the opportunity large. Albina, Rip City broadcast lore, maker craft and supporter culture give unusually deep design material. headline: Sacramento saved its Kings. Sell the city purple, a little bridge bronze and the Beam.

archetype.name: The Keepers
archetype.description: A fan base that personally rescued its team and treats every home game as civic duty. It forgives losing, not condescension, and punishes anything that reads as Bay Area, Lakers or outsider.

pulse.teamMoment: A youth movement after a 22-60 season and a lost lottery tiebreak. No. 7 pick Darius Acuff Jr. joins Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine and Malik Monk under Doug Christie, now in his second full season. There's no opening-night or Christmas Day game, and the Cup group brings the Spurs, Lakers, Warriors and Trail Blazers.
pulse.sentiment: Patient, defiant and a little sour. Fans are tired of losing and wary of the roster. But they quote the "going to be bad" forecasts back with a chip on their shoulder, and they're ready to back Acuff, Sabonis and Christie.

verifiedMoment: A youth movement led by No. 7 pick Darius Acuff Jr., with holdovers Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine and Malik Monk. Sacramento is widely projected near the bottom of the West.

scorecard.rationale: Fans who saved the team keep fandom just above average, and Specter is the main national hook. A likely bottom-West season, a value-leaning Valley and a lighter design well than its California neighbors put Sacramento near the floor on the other three axes (brief scores: opportunity 52, culture 63, retail 44, fandom 70). Loyalty runs well above league average because fans saved the team, and the bridge, the Beam and the neighborhood scenes give real design material. Three things hold opportunity and retail near or below average: a likely bottom-West season (fewer home wins, softer attendance), a value-leaning Valley, and no full-price Nike door or dense boutique scene.

headline: San Antonio wears silver and black every day, and Fiesta color on the days that count.

archetype.name: The Civic Family Contender
archetype.description: A multigenerational, Latino-majority, military-heavy fan base that spans the West, East and South Sides. It treats the Spurs as the city's shared family table and prizes humility over flash. After losing the 2026 Finals, it now expects a title.

pulse.teamMoment: The Spurs won the West in 2026 at 62-20, beating OKC 4-3 in the West finals, then lost the Finals 4-1 to the Knicks. They extended Wembanyama (5 years, $252M) and Fox through 2029-30. The core runs it back under Mitch Johnson, and they're title co-favorites with OKC. Opening night, Oct 20, is the West finals rematch with OKC. The Knicks come back on Christmas Day at MSG and on Mar 7 in San Antonio.
pulse.sentiment: Confident and hungry, not celebratory. Fans are proud of the West title, stung by the Knicks and protective of Spurs humility. They watch Project Marvel and the Frost Bank Center lease talks with civic interest, not alarm.

verifiedMoment: The 2026 West champions and Finals runners-up run it back after locking up Victor Wembanyama and De'Aaron Fox. They're title co-favorites with OKC. Downtown-arena planning for Project Marvel goes on.

scorecard.rationale: A title co-favorite led by Wembanyama, in a one-team region that runs to Mexico, puts fandom and opportunity near the top. Retail is ordinary mall-and-Academy volume, and the Fiesta and West Side culture is distinctive but narrower than the coastal giants' (brief scores: opportunity 82, culture 86, retail 56, fandom 90). Opportunity, culture and fandom run well above average. The Spurs are title co-favorites led by Wembanyama, in a one-team region that runs to Mexico. They have some of the league's most specific design material: Fiesta, conjunto, West Side craft and the East Side's Iceman lineage. Retail is ordinary: mall, Academy and arena-store volume in a price-aware market, with a thin independent sneaker scene and a real bootleg channel.

headline: Utah buys Jazz gear statewide, five kids at a time, dressed for the canyon and measured against Stockton and Malone.

archetype.name: The Statewide Family Loyalist
archetype.description: A fan who drives in on I-15 with three kids in purple youth jerseys and measures every new star against Stockton and Malone. The January walk to the Delta Center is cold, so it's a puffer and a beanie. Loyal to the team over any brand, patient with a rebuild, allergic to hype.

pulse.teamMoment: Coming off 22-60, Utah is speeding up its youth movement. No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey join Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. Walker Kessler went to the Lakers for future firsts, and Jaxson Hayes and Josh Okogie came in. Will Hardy is under pressure to develop them, and BetMGM's 35.5-win total asks for about 13 more wins.
pulse.sentiment: Impatient but curious. Fans are tired after a bottom-of-the-league year and energized by Peterson and the Jackson Jr. trade. They expect visible progress and a play-in chase, not a playoff run.

verifiedMoment: Utah's youth movement speeds up. No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey play next to veterans Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr., and Will Hardy is under pressure to develop them.

scorecard.rationale: Whole-state, family-sized loyalty keeps fandom near the league average. A small metro in a rebuild, with no national stage and a thin boutique layer, sits near the bottom on opportunity, culture and retail (brief scores: opportunity 52, culture 66, retail 40, fandom 68). A small metro, but the buyer base is the whole state: family-sized, youth-heavy and loyal to one team. Its design vocabulary is unusually distinct (salt, snow, all-ages DIY, West Side hoops). Retail is spread along I-15 with a thin boutique layer, and a rebuild year with no national stage caps the near-term upside.
